==English== {{wp|}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|contree|countrey||archaic}} * {{alter|en|contrey|countre|countrie|counterie||obsolete}} * {{alter|en|counthry||pronunciation spelling}} * {{alter|en|cuntry||eye dialect|derogatory}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:contre>>|tree=1|text=++}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|kintra}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|county}}. Displaced native {{m+|en|land}} in some of its senses. From around 1300 as "area surrounding a walled city or town; the open country." By early 16th century the sense was applied mostly to rural areas, as opposed to towns and cities. Compare typologically {{m+|ru|страна́}}, {{m|ru|сторона́}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|kŭn'tri}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌntɹi/|[ˈkʰʌnt̠ɹ̠̊˔ʷi]|a=RP,US,CA}} *** {{audio|en|en-uk-country.ogg|a=UK}} *** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-country.wav|a=GA}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-country.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌntɹɪj/|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkʊntɹi/|a=Northern England,Midlands}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌntɾe/|/-tɾɪ/|/-tɾi/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌntɾi/|a=Wales}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkɐntɹi/|a=AuE,NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkən.ʈɾi/|[ˈkɜn.t̺riˑ]|a=Indic}} ** {{rhymes|en|ʌntɹi|s=2}} * {{enPR|koun'tri|a=common for [[ESL]] speakers|q=proscribed}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈkaʊntɹi/}} ** {{rhymes|en|aʊntɹi|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|coun|try}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|territory of a nation; nation state; sovereign state}} The territory of a [[nation]]; a [[sovereign state]] or a [[region]] once independent and still distinct in [[institutions]], [[language]], etc. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:country}} #: {{hypo|en|LMIC|HIC|developing country|developed country|member country|mini-country|old country|Thesaurus:country}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1935|author=[https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/288354.George_Goodchild George Goodchild] |title=Death on the Centre Court|chapter=5 |passage=By one o'clock the place was choc-a-bloc. {{...}} The restaurant was packed, and the promenade between the two main courts and the subsidiary courts was thronged with healthy-looking youngish people, drawn to the Mecca of tennis from all parts of the '''country'''.}} #* {{quote-av|en|author= w:Michael Parenti|date= 15 April 1986|location= {{w|Boulder, Colorado|Boulder}}, {{w|Colorado}} |title= U.S. interventionism, the Third World, and the USSR |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xP8CzlFhc14&t=173s|time= 02:53 |text= But that expropriation of the Third World, [that] has been going on for 400 years, brings us to another revelation: namely, that the Third World is not poor. You don't go to poor '''countries''' to make money. There are very few poor '''countries''' in this world. Most '''countries''' are rich: the Philippines are rich, Brazil is rich, Mexico is rich, Chile is rich; only the people are poor. But there's billions to be made there, to be carved out, and to be taken; there's been billions for 400 years! The Capitalist European and North American powers have carved out and taken the timber, the flax, the hemp, the cocoa, the rum, the tin, the copper, the iron, the rubber, the bauxite, the slaves, and the cheap labour. They have taken out of these '''countries'''. These '''countries''' are not underdeveloped; they're overexploited!}} #* {{RQ:Mandela Long Walk to Freedom|year=2010|page=3|passage=It is a beautiful '''country''' of rolling hills, fertile valleys, and a thousand rivers and streams which keep the landscape green even in winter.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68 |url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time|title=T time |passage=The ability to shift profits to low-tax '''countries''' by locating intellectual property in them, which is then licensed to related businesses in high-tax '''countries''', is often assumed to be the preserve of high-tech companies.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702223329/http://www.economist.com:80/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time|archivedate=2 July 2017}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Lilit Marcus|title=This country has a national happiness index. But what is it really like to live there?|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/life-in-bhutan-intl-hnk/index.html|date=2024-07-04|passage=Most foreigners who have heard of Bhutan know two things: the '''country''' charges international visitors a $100/day sustainable development fee (aka tourist tax), and that it is the birthplace of the Gross National Happiness Index, a system intended to look after the well-being of citizens and the environment.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724100055/https://www.cnn.com/travel/life-in-bhutan-intl-hnk/index.html}} # A large area regarded as distinct from other areas, e.g. because it is inhabited by a specific group of people #: {{ux|en|[[Basque Country|Basque '''Country''']]}} # {{senseid|en|area, district, region}} {{lb|en|especially|_|Britain|uncountable|countable}} An [[area]] of land of undefined extent; a [[region]], a [[district]]. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=David Vann|journal=w:The Observer|date=2010-03-07 |passage=We walk along flat, open '''country''', red dirt and spinifex grass, a few short trees{{nb...}}.}} ## {{senseid|en|region of land delimited by certain factors}} {{lb|en|uncountable|countable}} An [[area]] of land of indefinite extent or of more or less definite extent in relation to human occupation, especially characterized by its particular [[physical]] [[features]], or its suitability for a particular [[activity]] or connected with its [[population]] (by [[race]], [[dialect]], [[culture]], etc.) or a [[person]], especially a writer, or their [[works]]. ##: {{hypo|en|backcountry|high country|north country|upcountry}} ##: {{uxi|en|Thomas Hardy '''country'''}} ##: {{ux|en|Hikers love the wild '''country''' that lies northwest of this river confluence.}} ##: {{ux|en|Since this was rebel '''country''', checkpoints were set up along the road.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|author=Chris Moss|journal=w:The Guardian|date=2007-02-17 |passage=This is condor '''country''' – the only region this far east where you can see the magnificent vulture – and a small national park straddling the passes, El Condorito, is a good stopover for walkers and birders.}} # {{senseid|en|the country, rural area, as opposed to the town or city}} {{lb|en|uncountable|usually preceded by “the”}} A rural area, as opposed to a [[town]] or [[city]]; the [[countryside]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} #* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=17|book=II|passage=I was borne and brought up in the '''Countrie''', and amidst husbandry{{nb...}}.}} #* {{quote-av|en|date=September 12 1999|author={{w|Anthony Horowitz}}; et al|chapter=Dead Man's Eleven|title={{w|Midsomer Murders}} |passage=''Joyce Barnaby:'' You don't kill someone because they made you [[redundant]].
''DCI Tom Barnaby:'' Not in the town, dear, but this is the '''country'''. And, in the '''country''', [[anything goes]].}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=4 Mar 2000|author=Alexander Chancellor|journal=The Guardian |passage=I have always thought that one of the main reasons for the popularity of blood sports in the '''country''' is the pointlessness of going outdoors with no purpose or destination in mind.}} #* {{quote-book |en |url=https://archive.org/details/englishpenguindictionaryofliterary/Difficulties_in_Learning_English_as_a_Se/ |year=2006 |month=May |author=James B. Weld |title=Difficulties in Learning English as a Second or Foreign Language |publisher=w:Regis University |page=37 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/englishpenguindictionaryofliterary/Difficulties_in_Learning_English_as_a_Se/page/n40/ |passage=She grew up in Chang-hua, a city in central Taiwan with a decidedly '''country''' flavor.}} #: {{ux|en|I grew up in the '''country''' with a 12-gauge shotgun.}} # The [[inhabitants]] or [[people]] of a [[district]], [[region]], or [[nation]]; the [[populace]], the [[public]]. {{defdate|from ca. 1300}} #: {{co|en|a scandal that rocked the '''country'''}} # {{senseid|en|traditional lands of Indigenous people}} {{lb|en|Australia|usually capitalised}} [[traditional|Traditional]] lands of [[Indigenous]] people with [[embed]]ded [[cultural]], [[spiritual]], [[cosmological]], [[ecological]], and [[physical]] attributes and values. #* {{RQ:Guardian|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007031547/https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2015/mar/11/of-three-remote-communities-here-why-are-only-the-two-aboriginal-ones-under-threat|author=Calla Wahlquist|title=Of three remote communities here, why are only the two Aboriginal ones under threat?|date=11 March 2015|passage=Milgin says living on '''country''', with elders, makes Aboriginal people "strong". That's backed up by a 2011 report on Aboriginal homelands by Amnesty International that found that living on homelands was connected to better health outcomes and drug rehabilitation.}} # {{senseid|en|country music, elliptically}} {{ellipsis of|en|country music}}. {{defdate|from 20th c.}} #: {{ux|en|a '''country''' song}} #: {{ux|en|a '''country''' singer}} #: {{ux|en|a '''country''' festival}} # {{senseid|en|spirit of country folkways}} {{lb|en|informal}} The [[spirit#Noun|spirit]] of the [[#English:_the country, rural area, as opposed to the town or city|country]] (rural places): the spirit of country [[folkway]]s; those folkways. #: {{collocation|en|You can take the boy out of the country, but you can't take the '''country''' out of the boy.}} # {{senseid|en|rock through which a vein of ore or coal runs}} {{lb|en|mining}} The [[rock]] through which a [[vein]] of [[ore]] or [[coal]] runs. #: {{cot|en|gangue#Noun|overburden#Noun}} ====Usage notes==== The geographical sense of "country" usually refers to a [[sovereign state]], that is, a nation with no administrative dependence on another one, which is the definition adopted in most world maps. In a broader sense, however, "country" may also refer to polities, or their territories, with some degree of autonomy and cultural identity but still under the sovereignty of another state. Examples of the latter include [[Scotland]], [[Tibet]], [[Abkhazia]], and [[Greenland]]. Such usage may be interpreted as supporting [[secessionism]] of these polities by others. ====Derived terms====
